## Core idea

Scientific calculators usually have an exponent-entry key labelled something like **EXP**, **EE**, or **×10ˣ**.

To enter **4.7 × 10⁻⁶**, enter the coefficient 4.7, use the exponent key, then enter −6.

The exponent key represents the **× 10ⁿ** part. It is different from multiplying by 10 with the ordinary multiplication key.

Calculator displays vary, so check how your calculator shows scientific and engineering notation.

## Class check

Before trusting the display:

- identify the coefficient;
- identify the exponent;
- check the sign of the exponent;
- ask whether the size of the answer makes sense.
